info.title: Wasla CRM API
info.description:
Wasla CRM — Comprehensive API for multi-tenant service businesses.

**Portal user lifecycle:**
Register (Digital Signature) → Lead (no company) → Submit Service Request (to any company) → Company Conversion → Customer (company-scoped).

**JWT claims:**
- `leadId` — present when user is a Lead.
- `customerId` — present once converted/accepted by at least one company.

**Multi-tenancy:** all company-scoped endpoints resolve CompanyId from the JWT.

post.summary: Authenticates a user and returns a JWT token.
post.description:
This endpoint is the primary gateway for all user roles (Individual, Manager, Employee, SuperAdmin).

**Business Logic:**
- If the user belongs to a company, it validates the company status (Pending/Active/Rejected).
- Multi-tenancy is enforced via the `CompanyId` claim embedded in the returned JWT.
- Access is denied (403) if the company is not yet activated or has a rejected status.

200.description: Successfully authenticated. Returns JWT and user role/permissions.

403.description: Business-level access denial (Company pending activation, subscription expired, or registration rejected).

post.summary: Change the password for the currently authenticated user.
post.description:
Requires a valid JWT. The user must supply their current password along with
the new password (and its confirmation). On success all existing refresh tokens
are revoked, forcing re-authentication on other devices.

400.description: Validation error or current password is wrong.

post.summary: Request a one-time password (OTP) to reset a forgotten password.
post.description:
Always returns 200 OK to prevent email enumeration. If the email exists, a
6-digit OTP valid for 10 minutes is sent.

**Rate limit:** 5 requests per 60 seconds per IP.

200.description: Request processed (OTP sent if email is registered).

post.summary: Reset a forgotten password using the OTP received by email.
post.description:
The OTP is valid for 10 minutes and can be used only once. After 5 incorrect
attempts the OTP is permanently invalidated.

**Rate limit:** 5 requests per 60 seconds per IP.

400.description: Invalid OTP, expired OTP, or password policy violation.

post.summary: Resend a new OTP for password reset.
post.description:
Invalidates any previous active OTP and issues a fresh one.
Always returns 200 OK to prevent email enumeration.

**Rate limit:** 5 requests per 60 seconds per IP.

200.description: Request processed (new OTP sent if email is registered).

post.summary: Registers a new company and its initial manager user.
post.description:
This is the self-service onboarding entry point for new service businesses.

**Workflow:**
1. Creates a `Company` record with status `Pending`.
2. Creates the `Manager` user account for the person submitting the form.
3. Assigns the `Basic` subscription plan by default.
4. The company will NOT be able to login until a SuperAdmin approves the registration.

**Constraints:**
- Company name and contact email must be unique.
- Manager email must not already be in use by another user account.

requestBody.description: Full company registration and manager contact details.

201.description: Registration received successfully. Company is now in `Pending` state.

400.description: Validation errors (e.g., invalid email format, missing required fields).

409.description: Conflict (Company name or email already exists).

post.summary: Registers a new portal user account (creates a Lead).
post.description:
Registering creates a **Lead** record — a user who is not yet linked to any company.
A unique **Digital Signature** is automatically generated for the lead upon registration.
            
The response JWT will contain a `leadId` claim but **no** `customerId` yet.
To become a Customer of a specific company, the lead must submit a **Service Request**
to that company. The company will then convert the inquiry into a customer account.
            
The response also includes a `refreshToken` and `refreshTokenExpiry` (short-lived, 1 day).

201.description: Lead account created. Returns JWT token, refresh token, and user info.

400.description: Validation errors (invalid email, password too short, etc.).

post.summary: Authenticates a portal user and returns a JWT token plus a refresh token.
post.description:
The returned token may contain:
- `leadId` — if the user is a Lead.
- `customerId` — if the user has been accepted/converted by at least one company.
- Both claims — once a lead has a customer record in one or more companies.
            
The response also includes the user's unique **Digital Signature**, which is required 
to accept offers.
            
Check which claim is present to determine the user's state and which portal
endpoints are available.
            
**Refresh token**: The response includes a `refreshToken` and `refreshTokenExpiry`.
Use `POST /refresh-token` to exchange a valid refresh token for a new access token without re-entering credentials.
            
**Remember Me**: Set `rememberMe: true` for a long-lived refresh token (30 days).
When omitted or `false`, the refresh token expires in 1 day.

200.description: Login successful. Returns JWT, refresh token, and user info.

401.description: Invalid email or password, or account is inactive.

400.description: User is not linked to a lead or customer record.

post.summary: Exchanges a valid refresh token for a new access token and rotated refresh token.
post.description:
Implements secure token rotation:
- Each refresh token can only be used **once**.
- If a previously-used token is sent again (replay), the entire token family is revoked.
- The old refresh token is invalidated; a new one is returned.

200.description: New access token + rotated refresh token.

401.description: Invalid, expired, revoked, or replayed refresh token.

post.summary: Logs out the current session by revoking the provided refresh token (and its rotation family).
post.description:
The client should discard the access token locally.
This endpoint is idempotent — calling it with an already-revoked token returns 204.

post.summary: Logs out from **all devices** by revoking every active refresh token for the current user.

get.summary: Retrieves a paginated list of companies registered on the platform.
Retrieves a public paginated list of recommended companies ranked by weighted composite score.
get.description:
Ranking uses deduplicated latest-per-customer reviews, Bayesian weighting, and recency decay.
Results can be filtered by service type and are returned in descending recommendation order.

400.description: Invalid page index or page size.

get.summary: Retrieves a public paginated list of trending companies with significantly improving recent reviews.
get.description:
Trending requires at least 2 deduplicated reviews in the last 90 days and
a recent-average improvement of at least 0.5 stars over the all-time average.
Results are sorted by improvement delta descending with review count as tiebreaker.

200.description: Returns a paginated trending companies result.

400.description: Invalid page index or page size.

- If called by a Lead, a Customer record is automatically created or found for that Lead + Company pair.
- If called by a Customer, the existing Customer record is used directly.

get.description:

This endpoint returns personal details plus a list of all company connection requests
(Pending / Accepted / Rejected) sent by this lead.
            
Use `GET /my/profile` instead once the lead has been accepted and has a `customerId`.

The system automatically identifies the company from the authenticated user's token.

tags.name: 01 - Authentication & Onboarding
tags.description: Entry points for user login and new company registration flow. Multi-tenancy begins here.

tags.name: 02 - Customer Portal
tags.description:
Public and customer-authenticated endpoints for the self-service portal.

**User lifecycle:**
1. `POST /register` → creates a **Lead** (no company link). A unique **Digital Signature** is generated. JWT contains `leadId`.
2. Lead browses companies and submits a **Service Request** to a company.
3. Company manager processes the request → a **Customer** record is created. JWT gains `customerId`.
4. Customer can now access offers, service requests, reviews, and dashboard.

A lead can connect to **multiple** companies; each produces a separate Customer record.

tags.name: 03 - Company Management
tags.description: Manager-level operations for company settings, logos, service catalog, and high-level dashboard metrics.

tags.name: 04 - Company Operations
tags.description:
Core day-to-day business operations for managers and employees.

**Includes:**
- **Offers** — Create multi-service quotes (optionally from a Service Request), send PDFs, and track status (Pending → Sent → Accepted/Rejected). Customers accept via **Digital Signature** in the portal.
- **Tasks** — Full lifecycle management (Pending → InProgress → Completed) with reassignment, audit trails, and time tracking.
- **Customers** — Company-scoped customer records. Customers can also be auto-created when a Lead submits a Service Request.
- **Employees** — Workforce management with performance analytics and task history.
- **Expenses** — Financial tracking with category/date filtering and charting.
- **Appointments** — Schedule site visits with optional Google Calendar sync.

tags.name: 05 - Integrations
tags.description: External service connections like Stripe payment gateway settings.

tags.name: 06 - SuperAdmin
tags.description: Global system administration: approving companies, managing subscription plans, and platform-wide metrics.
